newsitem.title: JAPAN: KASHIMA ROUT NAGOYA 7-0 TO STAY AT J-LEAGUE TOP.
newsitem.headline: KASHIMA ROUT NAGOYA 7-0 TO STAY AT J-LEAGUE TOP.

text.p: The Kashima Antlers, Japan soccer's J-League first-stage champions, thrashed Nagoya 7-0 on Saturday to remain unbeaten in the second stage of the championships.
Hisashi Kurosaki opened the scoring with a header in the 32nd minute and followed up with another seven minutes later, helping the Antlers to a comfortable 4-0 lead at half-time.
Brazilian Mazinho delighted a home crowd of 17,000 by chalking up two late goals, taking his tally this season to 13 in a game the Antlers never looked like losing.

With the victory, Kashima vastly improved their goal difference to keep up the pressure on league leaders Iwata, who also maintained their 100 percent record with a 4-1 victory at Cerezo Osaka. Iwata have played one game more than Kashima.
Toshiya Fujita and Takashi Fukunishi had Iwata 2-0 up by the 20th minute and Masashi Nakayama later added a third for his fourth goal in three matches.
In Yamagata, Yokohama Marinos' Spanish striker Julio Salinas demolished Kawasaki's defence with four strikes in his team's 7-2 victory. It was Kawasaki's seventh league defeat.
Marinos forward Shoji Jo, who has earned an international recall for Japan's home friendly against Brazil next Tuesday, found the net twice, his first goals since tearing a thigh muscle in late May.
Masahiro Fukuda scored two second-half goals in the space of two minutes as Urawa came back to beat hosts Hiroshima 2-1.
In Hiratsuka, international midfielder Hidetoshi Nakata and Brazilian Claudio took Bellmare to a 2-1 win over Kyoto.
Cameroon forward Patrick Mboma broke a 1-1 deadlock with a 67th minute goal to give Gamba Osaka a 2-1 victory away at Shimizu.
Yokohama Flugels' Valber drew level with league top scorer Edilson after his two brought his total to 17 this season and earned his team a 3-2 victory away at Kobe.
Lowly Fukuoka managed one point by downing mid-table Kashiwa on penalties after the two teams ended extra time at 1-1.
